title: Hat guessing with proper colorings
summary: We initiate the study of the hat guessing number of a graph where the adversary is only allowed to provide a proper coloring of the graph. This is the largest number $q$ for which there is a guessing strategy on each vertex that only depends on its neighborhood, such that for every proper coloring of the graph with $q$ colors at least one vertex guesses its color correctly. In this variation, we prove that the hat guessing number of the complete graphs on $n$ vertices is $2n - 1$, which is roughly twice the classical hat guessing number of the complete graph.
